Delivery objective: Remove uncertainty before building product features.
Demonstrable outcome: One real read-only OpenShift investigation runs through ADA and the existing MOSAIC runtime, with the response streamed to a minimal client.
Parallel work: Web shell and access API contract can begin against recorded interfaces.
Exit criteria: ADA interfaces and persistence are confirmed. Git and JSON startup configuration is pinned. The end-to-end path works.

Delivery objective: Put a safe, usable conversation path in front of invited development users.
Demonstrable outcome: A provisioned Human Account can call the API or use the web application to create a Session, submit a prompt and receive an SSE response.
Parallel work: Access API and web application proceed in parallel after the API contract is agreed.
Exit criteria: Development-token authentication, Session ownership, REST and SSE work together. No administration UI is required.

Delivery objective: Give each Account its own Sessions and enabled Public Skills without replacing the current catalogue or snapshot mechanisms.
Demonstrable outcome: Two users can browse Public Skills, enable different Skills, run separate investigations and continue only their own Sessions.
Parallel work: Catalogue UI can begin from Git metadata while persistence and ownership mappings are built.
Exit criteria: Account isolation passes. New Accounts start with no Skills. Changes apply to the next Goal and do not change in-flight work.

Delivery objective: Make the narrow release repeatable and operable in the development environment.
Demonstrable outcome: The complete controlled pilot can be demonstrated, redeployed and supported with explicit limitations.
Parallel work: Read-only verification, operational checks and release documentation can start earlier.
Exit criteria: Pilot checklist passes with two Accounts. Providers remain read-only. Known exclusions and replacement paths are documented.
